decisions.reason: As a flagship product line tightly tied to the firm's core software and digitalisation strategy, management would likely tolerate mixed short-run results and keep adapting it unless it clearly falls below aspirations.

Because the education institute builds on existing training content and customer relationships, it is a complementary offering that a growing firm with some slack would usually retain unless performance persistently disappoints.

The remote support tool fits the established support business and can be sustained at relatively low search and coordination cost, so management would be inclined to keep it while learning about usage.
A practice analytics dashboard is close to the firm's core product logic and future direction, so even if uptake is uneven the firm would more likely refine than withdraw it.

The complete practice bundle is very close to the established offer and likely supports cross-selling and customer retention, which lowers the chance that management reallocates its resources away from it.

The job and practice listing portal is comparatively distant from the firm's core competencies and, if it falls short of aspirations, behavioral-theory logic suggests management would redirect resources to closer and more proven activities.
